_comment: Hand corrections to the OCR pass, folded in by tools/build_coords.py.
Positions are pixels of .build/a21/drawing_full.png (5860 x 3580) for the
board and of .build/a21/schN_full.png (6380 x 3900, all five sheets) for
the sheets -- NOT of the downscaled images the browser loads. Every x,y is
a box centre.
How this board read. The drawing gave 99 of 137 designators and 20 of
those were wrong -- almost all of them a label read off the neighbour
(C1 on C7, C3 on C30, C5 on C49, C70 on C10, U17 on U11, R1 on R13, Q1 on
VR2, L1 on TP10, K4 on C44, J4 on J1, J11 on C47, S1 on J2, X8 on C16) or
off a word of silkscreen (U1 on UNGUARDED, R23 on RS232C, W1 on the 1988
copyright, MP7 on U9's notch, J6 on the '16' of C16). Every marker was
rendered onto the drawing and looked at, and every part on the board is
placed by hand below, measured off a 100 px grid over the full-resolution
image, so nothing on the board is left to the reader.
Marker style. Where the designator is printed inside the part's outline --
the twelve relays, the DIP ICs, the connectors, the fuses, the resistors
and capacitors of the TP6-TP7 row and the round cans C10, C16 and C70 --
the box is the printed body outline ('shape': 'rect' or 'circle'). Where
it is printed beside the part the box is a tight fit on the designator
text only. Test points are wire loops (a bare tick) or rectangular pads
(TP11, TP12, TP14, TP15); each box spans the label and the loop or pad
together so a probe is sent to the pad and not to the lettering.
Sheets. The five sheets of 5700A-1009 were reviewed marker by marker; the
test point legend, the IC supply-pin table and the connector location
tables on sheet 1 are dropped wholesale and each test point is placed on
its flag symbol in the circuit body, in the zone the legend gives.
